prompt: Pack two 16-bit halves into a single int and pull them back out with shifts and masks, rejecting halves that do not fit in 16 bits.
explanation: Shifting left by 16 moves a value into the top half of an int, and | drops the second value into the bits that shift left leaves as zeros. Unpacking reverses that: & 0xFFFF keeps only the bottom 16 bits, and >>> 16 slides the top half down while feeding in zeros instead of copies of the sign bit. Validating the halves up front is what keeps the packing reversible -- a value of 70000 would spill its extra bits into the other half and silently corrupt it.
hints: pack is one expression: (high << 16) | low, guarded by a range check that throws IllegalArgumentException.
low(packed) is just packed & 0xFFFF -- the mask removes everything above bit 15.
For high, use >>> so the sign bit does not get copied down, then mask with 0xFFFF for safety.
